p: Bath is a city that rewards a slow pace. You spend the day gazing at honey-coloured terraces, sipping tea and learning about Romans who came here for the hot springs. By evening, plenty of visitors are ready for something with a bit more noise, and that's where a games bar earns its keep. It gives a group a shared focus, which beats sitting round a table trying to decide what to do next.

Getting into the centre is simple. Bath Spa station is right by the SouthGate shopping area at the bottom of town, and the city is small enough that you can walk almost everywhere. Driving in can be slow at busy times and parking is tight, so many visitors use the park and ride sites on the edge of the city and leave the car outside.

Some tips for the night itself. Book your games before you start drinking, so you don't end up staring at an empty slot. Split into teams with a mix of confident players and nervous ones, and agree a forfeit before you begin, because it's far more fun when there's something on the line. Keep the scores fair, but don't be afraid of a bit of loud celebration either.

If you've got a bit of extra time, the Thermae Bath Spa offers a modern way to enjoy the city's famous warm water, with a rooftop pool that has a great view over the rooftops. Pair a relaxing soak with an evening of competitive games and you've got a cracking contrast for a weekend break.
